title: Defenders of the Realm - a long and casual discussion
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8OPlCKgcSO8

Daniel (@dungeondive) spends a rambling, tangent-strewn hour with *Defenders of the Realm* — Richard Launius's 2010 co-operative fantasy pandemic, set in the artistic world of Larry Elmore — and explains why his opinion of it has entirely reversed.

In 2010 the game sat awkwardly between two others. If the group wanted theme, stat tests and stories they played *Arkham Horror* second edition; if they wanted something quick and portable they played *Pandemic*. *Defenders* was longer and fiddlier than one and thinner than the other, so it stayed on the shelf. What changed is Daniel: he now plays almost entirely solo, and this is the game he reaches for when he wants a thematic *Pandemic*.

Much of the video is an unboxing of a clearance haul before the second edition arrives. The revised board, greener and higher-contrast; a full-size Quests of the Realm deck built partly from player submissions; demon minion replacements; Winds of War, which punishes you for playing your good special cards; Heroes Calling, which builds custom heroes from combat, control and movement abilities levelled in three stages; and Companions & Catacombs, which bolts an actual dungeon onto the overland map. He is blunt about the graphic design — Elmore's art is superb, the fonts and iconography are not — and notes the cardboard is the nicest he has ever held.

----

Have you ever had a game's stock rise years later purely because *you* changed — new group, solo play, different taste — rather than the game?
